recent_posts.title: New PCPJack worm steals credentials, cleans TeamPCP infections
recent_posts.summary: SentinelLabs has uncovered PCPJack, a new Linux-targeting worm that steals credentials from exposed cloud infrastructure including Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, MongoDB, and RayML. The malware actively removes competing TeamPCP infections from compromised systems, suggesting it was built by a former TeamPCP affiliate. PCPJack exploits several CVEs including Next.js auth bypass and WordPress plugin flaws, performs lateral movement via SSH key harvesting and Kubernetes enumeration, and exfiltrates encrypted credentials to Telegram. Mitigations include enforcing MFA, using IMDSv2 on AWS, and avoiding plaintext secret storage.

recent_posts.title: Australia warns of ClickFix attacks pushing Vidar Stealer malware
recent_posts.summary: Australia's Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) has issued a warning about an active ClickFix campaign targeting Australian organizations. Attackers compromise WordPress sites to redirect visitors to fake Cloudflare verification or CAPTCHA prompts, tricking users into manually running malicious PowerShell commands that install Vidar Stealer. This info-stealing malware-as-a-service targets browser passwords, cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, and system data. Vidar evades detection by deleting its executable post-launch and retrieving C2 addresses via public services like Telegram and Steam. ACSC recommends restricting PowerShell execution, implementing application allow-listing, and keeping WordPress themes and plugins updated.

recent_posts.title: Ivanti warns of new EPMM flaw exploited in zero-day attacks
recent_posts.summary: Ivanti has disclosed a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-6973) in Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) that is actively being exploited in zero-day attacks. The flaw stems from improper input validation and requires admin authentication to exploit, affecting EPMM 12.8.0.0 and earlier on-premises installations. Patches are available in versions 12.6.1.1, 12.7.0.1, and 12.8.0.1. Four additional high-severity EPMM vulnerabilities were also patched, though none of those have been observed exploited in the wild. Over 850 EPMM instances are currently exposed online. This follows a pattern of repeated EPMM zero-day exploitation, with CISA having flagged 33 Ivanti vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild to date.

recent_posts.title: The Browser Is Breaking Your DLP: How Data Slips Past Modern Controls
recent_posts.summary: Traditional DLP solutions have a critical blind spot: the browser. As enterprise workflows shift to browser-based apps like Google Workspace, GitHub, and AI tools such as ChatGPT, sensitive data increasingly moves through copy/paste actions, form inputs, AI prompts, and file uploads to unsanctioned accounts — all invisible to endpoint and network DLP. Analysis shows 46% of sensitive file uploads go to unsanctioned accounts. Browser-native DLP, as offered by Keep Aware, addresses this gap by operating directly within browsing sessions to inspect clipboard activity, form inputs, and uploads in real time, with full account and application context to enforce inline policies.

recent_posts.title: Americans sentenced for running 'laptop farms' for North Korea
recent_posts.summary: Two U.S. nationals, Matthew Isaac Knoot and Erick Ntekereze Prince, were each sentenced to 18 months in prison for operating laptop farms that helped North Korean IT workers fraudulently secure remote jobs at nearly 70 American companies. Knoot ran his operation from Nashville between 2022 and 2023, receiving company laptops under stolen identities and installing remote desktop software so North Korean workers could appear as legitimate U.S. employees. Prince operated through his company Taggcar Inc. from 2020 to 2024, enabling at least three North Korean workers to collect over $943,000 in salary, most of which was routed overseas. Combined remediation costs to victim companies exceeded $1.5 million. They are the seventh and eighth U.S.-based laptop farmers sentenced this year as part of a federal crackdown on North Korea's illicit IT worker schemes.

recent_posts.title: Palo Alto Networks firewall zero-day exploited for nearly a month
recent_posts.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed that suspected state-sponsored hackers have been actively exploiting CVE-2026-0300, a critical buffer overflow zero-day in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal (Captive Portal), since at least April 9, 2026. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution with root privileges on internet-exposed PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls. After successful compromise, attackers deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools and performed log cleanup to evade detection. The threat cluster (CL-STA-1132) is linked to likely state-sponsored actors, with EarthWorm previously associated with Chinese APT groups including Volt Typhoon and APT41. Over 5,400 PAN-OS VM-series firewalls are exposed on the internet. Patches are expected May 13; until then, Palo Alto strongly advises restricting or disabling the Authentication Portal. CISA has added the CVE to its KEV catalog and ordered federal agencies to remediate by May 9.

recent_posts.title: Fake Claude AI website delivers new 'Beagle' Windows malware
recent_posts.summary: A fake Claude AI website (claude-pro[.]com) is distributing a malicious installer disguised as a 'Claude-Pro Relay' tool for developers. Running the installer deploys a previously undocumented Windows backdoor called Beagle via a DonutLoader chain that uses DLL sideloading with a signed G Data executable. Beagle supports basic remote access commands and communicates with a C2 server over TCP/UDP using AES encryption. Sophos researchers found additional Beagle samples using different infection vectors, including impersonation of CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, and Trellix update sites. The campaign may be linked to PlugX operators experimenting with a new payload. Users should download Claude only from official sources and treat the presence of NOVupdate files as an indicator of compromise.

recent_posts.title: Hackers abuse Google ads for GoDaddy ManageWP login phishing
recent_posts.summary: A phishing campaign is abusing Google sponsored search results to target ManageWP credentials. The attack uses an adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) setup where a fake login page proxies credentials in real-time to the attacker, including 2FA codes, allowing full account takeover. Each compromised ManageWP account can expose hundreds of WordPress sites. Guardio Labs infiltrated the attacker's C2 infrastructure, found a private phishing framework with Russian-language disclaimers, and has identified at least 200 victims so far.

recent_posts.title: Critical vm2 sandbox bug lets attackers execute code on hosts
recent_posts.summary: A critical sandbox escape vulnerability (CVE-2026-26956) has been discovered in vm2, a widely-used Node.js sandboxing library with over 1.3 million weekly npm downloads. The flaw affects vm2 version 3.10.4 on Node.js 25 environments with WebAssembly exception handling and JSTag support enabled. Attackers can exploit WebAssembly's ability to intercept JavaScript errors at the V8 engine level, bypassing vm2's JavaScript-based protections. By triggering a crafted TypeError via Symbol-to-string conversion, a host-side error object leaks into the sandbox unsanitized, allowing access to Node.js internals like the process object and enabling arbitrary command execution on the host. A proof-of-concept exploit has been published. Users should upgrade to vm2 version 3.10.5 or later (latest: 3.11.2) immediately.

recent_posts.title: New Cisco DoS flaw requires manual reboot to revive devices
recent_posts.summary: Cisco has released security updates addressing a high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-20188) affecting Crosswork Network Controller (CNC) and Network Services Orchestrator (NSO). The flaw stems from inadequate rate limiting on incoming network connections, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to exhaust connection resources and crash affected systems with low-complexity attacks. Recovery requires a manual reboot. Cisco CNC 7.1 and earlier and NSO 6.4 and earlier are affected; users should upgrade to fixed releases. No active exploitation has been observed, though Cisco has a history of DoS vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.

top_posts.title: New npm supply-chain attack self-spreads to steal auth tokens
top_posts.summary: A new self-propagating supply chain attack has been discovered in the npm ecosystem, targeting packages from Namastex Labs. The malware, found in 16 compromised packages, steals developer credentials including npm publish tokens, API keys, SSH keys, cloud service credentials, CI/CD secrets, and cryptocurrency wallet data from browsers. Once it finds npm publish tokens on a compromised system, it injects itself into every package that token can publish and republishes them with an incremented version number, enabling recursive worm-like spread. It also targets PyPI if Python credentials are found, making it a multi-ecosystem threat. Developers using the listed package versions should remove them immediately, rotate all secrets, and audit CI/CD pipelines for indicators of compromise.

top_posts.title: Critical flaw in Protobuf library enables JavaScript code execution
top_posts.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability (GHSA-xq3m-2v4x-88gg) has been disclosed in protobuf.js, a JavaScript Protocol Buffers library with ~50 million weekly npm downloads. The flaw stems from unsafe dynamic code generation: the library builds JavaScript functions from protobuf schemas via string concatenation and the Function() constructor without validating schema-derived identifiers like message names. An attacker can supply a malicious schema to inject and execute arbitrary code, potentially gaining access to credentials, databases, and internal systems. Affected versions are 8.0.0/7.5.4 and below; patched versions 8.0.1 and 7.5.5 are available. A PoC exploit has been published, though no active exploitation in the wild has been observed. Mitigations include upgrading, auditing transitive dependencies, treating schema-loading as untrusted input, and using precompiled static schemas.

top_posts.title: Microsoft confirms April Windows updates cause backup failures
top_posts.summary: Microsoft has confirmed that April 2026 Windows security updates are causing failures in third-party backup applications that rely on the psmounterex.sys driver. The update adds this driver to Microsoft's Vulnerable Driver Blocklist to address CVE-2023-43896, a high-severity buffer overflow vulnerability enabling privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution. Affected products include Macrium Reflect, Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud, UrBackup Server, and NinjaOne Backup. Symptoms include VSS timeout errors, failed image-mount operations, and Code Integrity Event ID 3077 entries. Microsoft advises against uninstalling the update and recommends users upgrade to newer application versions that use updated, compliant drivers.

top_posts.title: April KB5083769 Windows 11 update causes backup software failures
top_posts.summary: The April 2026 KB5083769 security update for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2 is breaking third-party backup applications that rely on VSS (Volume Shadow Copy Service) snapshots. Affected products include Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud, Macrium Reflect, NinjaOne Backup, and UrBackup Server, all failing with a VSS timeout error during snapshot creation. As a temporary workaround, users can uninstall the KB5083769 update via Settings, pause Windows updates, and reboot. Microsoft has not yet issued an official fix. This follows other April 2026 update issues including Windows Server restart loops and BitLocker recovery prompts.

top_posts.title: Microsoft says Outlook.com outage is causing sign‑in failures
top_posts.summary: Microsoft is investigating an active Outlook.com outage causing intermittent sign-in failures, 'too many requests' errors, and unexpected sign-outs. Downdetector has received thousands of user reports since the incident began. Microsoft has classified it as 'service degradation' but has not yet disclosed the root cause, affected regions, or user count. The investigation is focused on client sign-in scenarios and interactions across service components.
